column1: # The mutations that show `just unity-android` can fail.
# `just unity-android-negative` applies each one to a COPY of the probe sources
# under `target/` and requires the recipe to go red naming the diagnostic in the
# `expect` column. `unity-conformance-negative` is the shape this follows, and
# issue #1370 is why it exists: these four had been run once and written into a
# commit message, and `implementing-a-change` rules that mutation evidence
# expires when a later round changes the code. It had already expired — the
# recorded evidence for `runtime-throws` said the recipe named R-E21, and by
# the time #1370 was filed the marker loop was exiting before that block.
# **Nothing here edits a committed file.** The mutation is applied to the copy,
# and `unity-android` takes its probe sources as its third parameter.
# Tab-separated, six columns, one mutation per line:
#   name      what to pass to the recipe; `all` runs every row
#   file      the probe source to mutate, relative to unity/android-probe/
#   find      the exact text to replace. It must appear exactly ONCE, and the
#             recipe refuses the row otherwise rather than running a mutation
#             that changed nothing
#   replace   what to put there. It may CONTAIN `find` — two of these wrap a
#             statement rather than deleting it — so the recipe confirms the
#             mutation by finding `replace`, not by failing to find `find`
#   expect    a literal the failing run must print. `unity/package-gate`'s
#             `android_probe_negative_control` holds each one to the file that
#             prints it, so a reworded diagnostic cannot leave this table
#             expecting text nothing emits
#   marker    the positive marker the mutation removes, or `-`. Two rows here
#             both end as "a marker never arrived", and without this column
#             they would be indistinguishable
# **Two rows for R-E8, and they reach different checks.** `r-e8-membership`
# defeats the probe's own read-back, which fails inside the editor before
# `BuildPlayer` is reached. `r-e8-fat-apk` makes the read-back agree and lets
# the build run, so the APK should carry both ABIs and the `unzip` refusal
# should turn the recipe red — the assertion the specification's R-E8 calls the
# strongest evidence any of these three requirements carries. Without the
# second row that assertion is exercised by nothing.
# **That last row is a PREDICTION, not a recorded run.** The others were run
# against a device; this one was added on 2026-08-29 and only its mutation was
# applied. If an ARMv7+ARM64 IL2CPP build fails in Gradle instead, the row
# reports "went red for some other reason", and its `expect` is what needs
# revising rather than the gate.
# Every row needs an editor with Android Build Support AND an attached device:
# `unity-android` refuses before it builds when there is none, so even the row
# that fails inside the editor cannot run without one.
